chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Muthannā al-Ḥannāṭ, from Abū Baṣīr, who said:

I entered upon Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), and I said to him, "Are you the heirs of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله)?" He said, "Yes." I said, "The Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) was the heir of the Prophets, and he knew all that they knew?" He said to me, "Yes." I said, "Then you are able to give life to the dead and cure the blind and the leper?" He said, "Yes, by the permission of Allah."

Then he said to me, "Come near to me, O Abū Muḥammad." So I came near him, and he wiped over my face and over my eyes, and I saw the sun, the sky, the earth, the houses, and everything in the town. Then he said to me, "Would you like to remain like this, with the same obligations and liabilities as the people upon the Day of Judgment, or return to how you were and have Paradise exclusively?" I said, "I return to how I was." So he wiped over my eyes, and I returned to how I was.
He said: Then I narrated this to Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, and he said, "I bear witness that this is true, just as the day is true."

key_terms.الْأَبْرَصَ: the leper, one afflicted with leprosy
key_terms.الْأَكْمَهَ: the blind, specifically one afflicted with blindness
key_terms.الْأَنْبِيَاءِ: the Prophets, whose knowledge is described as inherited by the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and then by the Imams
key_terms.بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ: by the permission of Allah, indicating that such acts occur only through divine authorization
key_terms.تُبْرِئُوا: to cure or heal, referring to miraculous healing
key_terms.تُحْيُوا الْمَوْتَى: to give life to the dead, mentioned here as occurring by Allah’s permission
key_terms.وَرَثَةُ: heirs or inheritors, referring here to the inherited authority and knowledge of the Imams
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ: the Day of Judgment, the day of reckoning and accountability

ai.seo_question: Can the Imams, by Allah’s permission, perform miracles such as healing the blind and reviving the dead?
ai.summary: This hadith presents Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) as inheriting the knowledge of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), who in turn inherited the knowledge of the Prophets. It also affirms, by the permission of Allah, extraordinary signs associated with the Imams, including healing and reviving the dead. The report further links such divine favor with accountability on the Day of Judgment and contrasts worldly capacity with the promise of Paradise.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Musna Al Hannat, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘I went over to Abu Ja’far<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>, so I said to him<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>, ‘You (Imams<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>) are the inheritors of the Prophets<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup>?’ He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’. I said, ‘Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> is an inheritor of the Prophets<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup>, knowing everything what they<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup> were knowing?’ He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said to me: ‘Yes’. I said, ‘So you (Imams<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>) are able upon reviving the death, and curing the blind and the leper?’ He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, by the Permission of Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>’.

Then he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said to me: ‘Approach me<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>, O Abu Muhammad!’ So I approached him<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>, and he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> wiped his<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> hand upon my face and upon my eyes. So I visualised the sun, and the sky, and the earth, and the houses, and everything in the city. Then he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said to me: ‘Would you love it to become like this, and for you would be what is for the people, and upon you would be what would be upon them on the Day of Judgment, or to return to just as you were, and for you would be the Paradise purely?’ I said, ‘To return to just as I was’. So he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> wiped upon my eyes, so I returned to just as I was’.
He (Abu Baseer) said, ‘So I narrated to Ibn Abu Umeyr with this, so he said, ‘I testify that this is true just as the day is true’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-Muthanna al-Hannat from abu Basir who has said the following. “

Once I went to see abu Ja‘far (a.s.) and asked him, “Are you the heirs of the Messenger of Allah?” He said, “Yes, we are his heirs.” I then asked, “Was the Messenger of Allah the heir of the prophets and knew all that they knew?” He said to me, “Yes, it is true.” I then asked, “Do you have the power to bring the dead back to life and cure the lepers, and the blind?” He said, “Yes, we do have such powers by the permission of Allah.”

The he said to me, “Come closer to me, O abu Muhammad.” I went closer to him and he rubbed my face and my eyes and saw the sun, the skies, the earth, the houses and all things in the town. Then he said to me, “Do you like to live this way and will have what others have and be responsible for whatever they will be held responsible on the Day of Judgment or like to live as before and will have paradise purely?” I said, “I would like to live as I lived before.” He rubbed my eyes and I found myself as before.”
The narrator has said that he told it to ibn abu ‘Umayr who said, “I testify that this is true just as the day is true.”
